basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Holds the engagement, its evidence and its conclusion, not the subject matter or the management assertion being examined.
Distinguishes audit (reasonable assurance), review (limited assurance) and agreed-upon procedures (factual findings without assurance).
Keeps practitioner findings, management responses and regulator decisions as separately sourced records.
An unmodified opinion is assurance in a stated scope, not a guarantee against fraud or error.

may: Organise workpapers, evidence references and procedures.
Run analytics and sampling to support procedures.
Draft findings and the management letter for practitioner review.
Track remediation actions and follow-up dates.
mustNot: Assert independence on behalf of the practitioner.
Waive evidence, sign off workpapers or form an opinion.
requiresHuman: Forming and signing the conclusion or opinion.
Deciding to report suspected fraud or noncompliance.

considerations: Third parties rely on assurance; an unsupported opinion misleads them.
Auditor independence protects the public interest and must not be compromised by convenience.
Workpapers contain confidential client and personal data.
affectedParties: Shareholders and other users of the report
Management and those charged with governance

items: An engagement has a practitioner, responsible party, subject matter, criteria, assurance level, period and report.
Often confused with an internal control assessment, a regulatory inspection and a consulting review.
Wrong opinion based on insufficient evidence.
Missing archive evidence when the opinion is challenged.
IAASB International Standards on Auditing (ISA) and ISAE 3000.
ISO 19011 guidelines for auditing management systems.
INTOSAI ISSAI framework for public-sector audit.
